beats.text: Sold as a slave. Then he wrote Don Quixote.
Remember the wounded soldier at Lepanto? Miguel de Cervantes, twenty-four. Two shots in the chest. A third ruined his left hand.
Four years later, sailing home, his galley was taken by pirates. He was sold as a slave in Algiers.
He tried to escape four times. Every time, he took the blame alone.
After five years, Trinitarian friars raised his ransom and bought him free.
Back home, he became a tax collector. Trouble with his accounts landed him in a Seville jail.
In the book's own prologue, he hinted it was born in a prison.
In 1605 it came out: an old man reads too many knight stories, and rides off to be a knight himself.
beats.say: In sixteen-oh-five it came out: an old man reads too many knight stories, and rides off to be a knight himself.

beats.text: He charges at windmills, sure they are giants. It was a hit at once. We still say tilting at windmills.
Cervantes died in April 1616. People say Shakespeare died the same day. He didn't. England used a different calendar.
beats.say: Cervantes died in April sixteen-sixteen. People say Shakespeare died the same day. He didn't. England used a different calendar.

beats.text: And this face? No one knows if it's really him. No portrait of Cervantes is known to be genuine.
But one painter made sure we would never forget his face.

beats.sub: Follow so you don't miss it
